reviews.title: Essential feature removed
reviews.text:
Please bring back the old station-to-station schedule view! One of the most useful features of the NJ TRANSIT app was being able to select two stations (e.g., Millburn → NY Penn), choose a future date, and simply see all scheduled trains for that route that day.

The new Trip Planner is not a replacement for this. It requires searching around a specific departure/arrival time and makes something that used to take seconds unnecessarily difficult. Commuters often need to look ahead at tomorrow’s schedule and quickly compare all of our options.

Please restore the ability to save/favorite a station pair and view the full schedule between those stations for any selected date. This was an incredibly useful, simple feature of the old app and I really hope you bring it back.

reviews.title: Updated look but downgraded user experience
reviews.text:
I have never written a review for  an app before. As a commuter and someone who RELIES on NJ Transit to get to work every day, I am here in the reviews hoping and praying that this gets seen so this app can be usable again. 

I will admit that this latest update has the previous version beat in terms of aesthetics. It has also integrated the departure vision and schedule toggles. 

This would be beneficial, if it worked consistently. That has been my greatest issue with this update: the app has not only removed helpful features like myBus and made it way harder to find things like train schedules, but it also just doesn’t work. 

I am a commuter, so I often buy bulk tickets (monthly pass, 10 ticket discount, flex pass, etc.), which makes commuting more cost effective. However, this app refuses to sign me in. I need to sign back in every morning, and before I can do that, I need to enter and exit and reenter the app at least 3 times before it lets me sign in or loads my ticket bundles. 

More than once, I have anticipated this lengthy sign in process and opened the app prior to boarding just to be signed out as I try to activate my ticket. It’s incredibly frustrating and costly because I have been in the position where I now need to buy a new ticket just to get to work or home. 

This was even worse during the World Cup. 

Please fix the app. Address the issue with sign in and loading ticket purchases. Bring back myBus, make it easier to find train schedules, fix the search bu

reviews.title: Underfunded joke of public transport has a terrible app, shocker
reviews.text: I wish I could give this app 0 stars. It is terribly designed. Firstly, they need to update it so transit riders can purchase a ticket without creating an account. I went to buy a ticket on my way to catch my train and tried to create an account, but it said my email had been used previously to purchase a ticket so I needed to finish setting up my account. I clicked to send the email to set up the account, and nothing. I clicked resend 3-4 times, still nothing. I had to purchase my ticket at the station’s kiosk (which was cash only? Does NJ transit just not want to take people’s money? Why is it so hard to buy a ticket). About 10 mins into my train ride, the email came through. The schedule part of the app is also confusing as someone who doesn’t take NJ transit every day and was trying to get there from NYC. I was trying to compare times to different stops and I had to keep clicking out, putting in the new destination, and the app doesn’t have a history option to show routes you previously looked up. I guess I shouldn’t be surprised that the underfunded joke that is NJ transit can’t shell out the funds to design an easy to use app.

reviews.text: NJ Transit is ruining lives. My card was removed from app, looks like $29 was added without my permission in a card balance. Where did that come from? I had deleted the app for a few days because of the enormous amount of storage that was being used. My credit card is gone from the app, which is disappointing. What’s the point of creating an account. On top of that, even when I press save details, the app signs me out everyday. The schedules are not consistent with Google and Apple Maps and I am just repeatedly frustrated with the service. The conductors I know are disappearing every ride and on top of that this fifa and back up path plans and canceling rides and the fires and the the lack of ac are appalling for the price us riders pay.

reviews.title: Worst update ever
reviews.text: If I could give this new update zero stars, I would. You removed features that helped riders navigate to their train and keep track of the timing for their current train. Why in any universe would you remove features that tell riders what track to go to for their train??!! How is that a helpful update?? Sprinting from the subway is stressful enough. Now I have to guess and pray I got the right track?? If you do nothing else, at least return that feature. If you have a soul and want to help why not also throw in the train tracker you threw out. Then riders can give somewhat accurate estimates on their arrival time to whoever was nice enough to pick them up from the train.

reviews.title: Update has NOT been helpful
reviews.text:
The way to see the train schedules is extremely annoying in that you can’t just choose a date, you also have to choose a time to depart or arrive by. So I have to arbitrarily choose a time to see the train options. 
ALSO, it’s currently 11:30PM and I’m trying to look at the train schedule for tomorrow, but when I follow the “Nearby & SCHEDULES -> Train” and I’m met with a pop up that tells me there’s no trains at this time and does not let me adjust the date to tomorrow! In what world is this helpful????? Using Trip Planner is somewhat of a workaround, but again you have to choose an arrival/departure time frame so you can only see like two train options at a time. 

Please. Take the feedback from actual train users.

reviews.title: Update does let you look at schedule at night
reviews.text: The way the update works, if your station doesn’t have anymore stops for the night, you can’t look at the schedule. Like, at all. Here’s what happens, in my case, it’s late and I want to look at tomorrow’s schedule. I select my home/origin station, and select Penn Station. Now because it’s late, a pop up says “there’s no trains tonight!” totally fine, except, it won’t let me look at tomorrow’s schedule. When I click OK on the pop up, it just takes me back. You are unable to select your departure date/time. Literally madness. The World Cup is tomorrow and I can’t look at schedules for tomorrow because there’s no trains “tonight.” Absolutely insane user experience with this update. It’s so bad. Just give us the schedule

reviews.title: planning is way harder with update
reviews.text:
Overall the new update looks cleaner but doesn’t seem to improve any functionality. One thing that’s really frustrating is that it’s difficult to just see the time tables without choosing a target departure/arrival time. If there aren’t currently trains running the route I’m trying to plan in advance I can’t even get to the screen where I tell the app what time of day I want to go because it gives me an error that there are no active trains running. I know they’re not running now, I’m not trying to go now. I’m trying to go in the morning but I can’t see what time the trains are because they’re not running right now.

Also this feature makes it impossible to see what time the train I’m currently on is estimated to get to a certain stop because I can’t look at the schedule for trains that have already left my station of origin 🤦‍♀️

reviews.title: New app does not provide accurate info
reviews.text:
BUGGY APP

After a few days, I thought they might update the app. No fixes implemented. 
While the schedule focuses on the departure times and station and in-train announcements also. Refer to trains by their departure times, departure vision no longer shows scheduled departure times. The app simply update the time when the train is late without no reference to the originally scheduled departure time at each station. 

When you want to search for schedules, it excludes trains that are close to the ‘departure at’ time. Horrible. 

Can’t find the schedules. Seems to only show departure vision. It was valuable to see schedule with the stops in between. That’s no longer available. 
On the departure vision page, it does not show the scheduled departure time. Most often passengers associate a train by the departure time. Not by the train number.

The favorites of Home and work don’t work. I have tried multiple times to save the starting station and destination station. But Everytime I choose either of them, it seems to pick the nearest address as the starting location and the current time. Instead of the saved locations and time.

Trip planner does not show all the train options. 
The previous app was far better. There was no need to upgrade to a buggy app.

reviews.title: Updated version is worse
reviews.text: You have to go through more of the app to finally view the bus schedules that you previously had marked as a favorite. Port Authority Bus Terminal gives me issues on viewing the next bus. I used to be able to favorite a route of a specific bus at a specific stop and view when the next bus would be arriving. Now you can't even do that. You favorite a route and it make you click on the bus stop just to show every single bus that goes to that specific bus stop instead of the one you're looking for. They need to update this recent update. Also there's no dark mode? Polish this asap! Trash. Before it was much better. Don't believe these bs 5 star reviews.

reviews.title: App Update is Horrible
reviews.text: The new app update might the worst design I have ever seen. I hope everyone responsible is fired. I can’t figure out if something is favorited because it puts a slash through it when I click to favorite. I can’t find a schedule for my route. I click to save my home location and it says there are no options when I live 5 min walking distance from a train. In about two minutes trying to find a schedule I encountered multiple bugs where my input was cleared or it showed buses when I only clicked to see trains. Did they even test the app? I literally cannot figure out how to find a schedule. The old app was bad, but at least it worked.

reviews.title: Bring Back “Current Train” Information
reviews.text:
The new app removed one of the most useful and underrated features: the ability to quickly see details about the train you’re currently riding. That feature made it easy to answer simple but important questions like, “Does this train stop at XYZ station?” or “Is this the correct train?”

Without it, riders are left guessing or scrambling to look up schedules while already onboard. I’ve lost count of how many times people relied on that information during a trip. Removing it adds unnecessary confusion and makes the app less practical for everyday commuters.

Please consider bringing this feature back. It genuinely improved the rider experience.

reviews.title: Bad to Worse
reviews.text:
I tried to get used to the new app layout and functions but it’s so hard. it’s hard to locate anything and I can’t save any of my favorite trips because it defaults to my current location when I search for a destination… 
I had one tap favorites that gave me the bus schedules… now I have to search every time and type in the origin and destination to get an accurate bus schedule. Also, my route has like 3 different busses that I can take home. After I search and see the bus times I have to click on the time to see which bus it is since they have the same route number but different routes. also there are busses with a letter suffix for like express or turnpike but the results only show the bus route by the main route. I have to click in each result to see which bus goes where. 

yea the UI is refreshed but all the functions have been made worse. what took 1 click before now takes a few clicks and typing and searching. Add that it automatically does a search once you click of the text makes it so much more frustrating. I’ve had to retype things so often because if this. this could have been avoided if the favorites still worked and i didn’t have to search for my route EVERY TIME.

please make this better. the fact that this updated right before the world cup makes it even more frustrating

reviews.title: Terrible Update!
reviews.text: This new update is incredibly difficult to use. I never had any issues before the redesign. It is difficult navigating to the train times of the locations I have favorited and it’s also not easy buying tickets. I normally only buy train tickets, but the app is now showing me I only have the option to buy light rail tickets. I ended up buying tickets through the NJ Transit website instead. What’s the point of having an app when your website is more reliable and accessible? This is an embarrassment of an app when we are literally minutes away from the world using our transit system for the World Cup. Do better NJ! And bring back the original app!

reviews.title: No longer functional
reviews.text: The old app was great and I’ve been using it for years without any problems. But unfortunately some moron manager who needed to justify his job decided to green light an app redesign and boy is it a stinker. The app doesn’t remember my login even though I opted in. The buy section doesn’t show all station stops. The only way to buy tickets is a convoluted series of taps through the schedules section which is impossible to find without guidance. And the cherry on top is bought tickets never show up in the my tickets section. It shows an error every time the ticket section is refreshed. NJ transit needs to revert this update because otherwise we get to be treated like criminals by the ticket gestappo even after showing email receipts of purchased tickets.

reviews.title: Old version fine. New version huge Charlie Foxtrot.
reviews.text:
The new version’s UI makes no sense (and no, I’m not just some cranky old person complaining about anything new). Train status is routinely out of date. Stations are listed in the wrong order and sometimes include stops that aren’t even on the same line. As in the displayed route and time sometimes aren’t just out of date, it’s physically impossible for a train to do without teleportation. 

Crashes/freezes while tickets are being activated/checked. I bought a ticket once that never even showed up, it just took my money. 

I take the train every day so I just roll my eyes and get on with it. But if I was a tourist, perhaps one who flew halfway around the world and paid thousands of dollars for tickets to a soccer match and need NJT to get there, a delay like that could very easily be like throwing my money down the drain. 

The old version was ugly but at least it worked. 

World Cup people: Do not rely on this app for information or to process your payment correctly! Buy paper tickets in advance at the station and if you’re remotely in doubt about where to go, as somebody. I don’t even trust they’ll put up signs.

reviews.title: Bus Schedule is Horrible
reviews.text:
With the new update I can’t load the 137 bus schedule going from Dorado to Port Authority. On top of that even when it does function properly it doesn’t show you the entire schedule like you can see on the rail schedule. It will only show you 3 route times within a window. It’s such a pain and will drastically change the results if you change your time by 10 minutes. I just want to see the entire days worth of trips in one place. But if that’s asking too much I’d just like to see the schedule in general. Right now I only see an error message saying My Bus error

An error has occurred while processing your request. Please retry in a few minutes.

reviews.title: Bring back the Schedules Feature!
reviews.text: The new app has some visual improvements, but the new “trip planner” is a significant downgrade on the old schedules feature, which listed all the upcoming travel options between two stations. Ironically, the old view was actually the detail you needed to plan a trip, as it allowed you to evaluate multiple potential departure times. The new trip planner makes you pick the time you plan to leave and only shows you the closest departure time, but it’s hard to say when you’ll leave if you don’t know what options are available. It also is incredibly slow and frequently crashes the app. The PDFs are still available for those who want schedules, but these are much harder to read and do not reflect cancellations or provide all available transfers.

reviews.title: Latest update got rid of most useful features (May 2026)
reviews.text:
Bring back the favorites home screen and let us fully customize the order of our favorites. The favorites screen was the most common screen used by frequent commuters. 
We don’t need an entire page of vague “system status” as the center home screen; have a separate notification screen to look at alerts/statuses. 
Make a setting to select how arrival times are shown, “7 min” vs “12:00 pm”. 
When selecting “view map” on a bus stop, the busses should show by default. 
Fix the filter for bus stops. The list is longer than the view window, and you cannot scroll to reach the top or bottom (PABT stop is worst). The routes should be sorted in some type of way, and should not have separate options for X, T,… lines. 
Make it so buttons can still be clicked even while the current data is being refreshed. Currently, if there is a slow internet connection, a user cannot back out or manually pull up their ticket until the current data finishes refreshing.

reviews.title: Terrible App
reviews.text: Outside of normal working days, no information on this app is accurate. At port authority in nyc, it shows the wrong gates for buses. On days with adjusted schedules, never rely on the information on this app. Apps should be an easy way for operators to feed schedule and gate changes, but NJ Transit doesn’t care about the confusion and wasted time is causes for its users. (But for a normal workday, I did not have any problems.) Also, sometimes the eticket doesn’t work, and once everyone on my commute line -people who use monthly tickets- had to pay separately for a one-way ticket using apple pay. No apologies or refunds from NJ Transit. I use it because there’s no alternative, but definitely tons of room for approval.

reviews.title: A poorly designed App by someone who does not understand how commuters could use this
reviews.text: The previous version of this App was inadequate. it is very surprising that the team was able to create a new version that is even worse. The app is designed by someone who does not use NJ Transit. The product team and UX team that came up with the design features are a really bad. If someone has this app building experience on their resume, do not hire them. This is a prime example of fancy looking app but poor and non intuitive fiunctionality. A simple process of identifying the list of trains between source and destination has been taken away and now you have to look at the PDF schedule. Just like the previous version, it is so annoying that everytime you open the app, the monthly pass or activated ticket pop up.

reviews.title: New fancy app, same old bs
reviews.text: Wowww so cool that you guys overhauled the app and introduced about 3 thousand new bugs onto it! But like. Can you guys actually work on your issues like not being able to access the stop or map info past a certain time of day or you know. Informing your customers when a scheduled bus isn’t going to arrive. Or actually giving updates when the trains are running incredibly behind! I was already stuck in RB for almost an hour; being stuck in SA for over 2 HOURS bc no one thought it pertinent enough to say “hey this bus is cancelled for xyz reasons” is frankly INSULTING to your customers. I’m tired of this, you can dress your app up all you want, it still does not change all the issues you and it have when you aren’t willing to actually address the real problems in the room.

reviews.title: New version is awful!! Something was working fOR NJT - why did they have to break it?!
reviews.text:
Most of NJT is a mess. But the app *was* good! Until mid May, when they forced a complete update. The new app is awful, fitting for NJT! Completely unintuitive, not helpful (how do we see departure vision?!) and my favorite - when do you find the screen that shows the tracks… the font size on the track number is minuscule. Boarding is written in large text. But is WHERE the boarding takes place easy to see? NO! And I say this as someone with 20/20 vision. 😝 Why was the app changed and WHY was it changed to this?! Was there testing? With users? Please make the tracks easier to see. Please make it more intuitive. How else will we see that our trains are delayed?!

Signed,
Wrote this while my train was delayed

reviews.title: New version of the app requires twice as many clicks to purchase a single ticket, please revert
reviews.text:
New version of the app requires twice as many clicks to purchase a single ticket, please revert

More details:

When you go to the payment screen there is a new click you need to do to select Apple Pay every time. After that once you go past the Apple Pay authorization there is a button on the app again to purchase the ticket. What is the rationale for that extra click? “Yes I am for sure still confident that I do still want to purchase this ticket even though I already told you so and went through Apple Pay authorization process already 5 seconds ago”?

The ticket activation experience could be better for people who buy a single ticket. Something like a single “buy and activate now” will be helpful. 

I also no longer could dons schedule timetables (in-app,not pdfs). Are they gone? Are they buried in the menus somewhere?

One good thing with the new version of the app is that the sound playback is no longer interrupted when the app is being used, so thank you for that.

reviews.title: New look, new problems
reviews.text: I’ll admit, the new app update looks better and surfaces a quick button to purchase a ticket, but this version has removed the single most useful function of the previous version. Ok, now I have dedicated buttons for my home location and my work location, cool. But the functionality of those only works if I am standing next to them at the moment, as the trip planner tries to pull a route from my exact location at the moment. I am never just trying to spit of the moment grab a train, I like most people, need to plan my route ahead of time. This removed the ability to save preferred routes and just pull up all of the scheduled times for that route on a given day. Now I must manually type in the route every time. This is backwards of how people want and need to use the app. Once again NJT doesn’t understand its own customers. Bring back the saved preferred routes!

reviews.title: Downgrade! I want the old app back
reviews.text: I use this app to view find out which track to board. 1) The track number’s font size is half of the old app. 2) swiping down does not refresh the track number. The track already came out, but the app doesn’t refresh unless I exit the page and completely reload the train station. 3) I haven’t figured out how to set my home and work locations. The fact that I need to search online and still cannot figure it out shows how unintuitive this is. 4) instead of the home screen, there is now a popup that starts off on my monthly pass. I want to get to the track information faster or set that as my default Home Screen. 5) my login expires daily after 24 hours. If this happens while cell service is unavailable, the conductor gives me trouble for not activating in advance. But I have no control over when this login expires! I can’t reset my login timer in advance while I had cell reception.

reviews.title: Only NJT can take an AWFUL app and make it WORSE!
reviews.text: So typical of NJT! What moron designed their new useless app? It’s impossible to assign favorite stations, you have to endlessly search to find the stations you need, information about your routes have completely disappeared, labels are completely meaningless (What in the hell does “station skipped“ mean? Apparently it means that the train has been canceled whether is a massive problem take other services such as the PATH which can add hours to the amount of time.) when trains are canceled you were stranded in New York City trying to get home, there are given note instructions as how to get back via PATH to Hoboken, which are listed on the new useless app, and then God knows what happens after that. That seems as if it was designed by a fifth grader.

reviews.title: F No
reviews.text:
Latest app update removed 3 important bits of functionality: (1) There is no way to discern what time a train you’re currently on will arrive at its destination. You can look this info up on train schedules before your train departs BUT if you don’t recall that info or if you caught a train last minute and didn’t have time to check, the train schedules and ride tools have removed your ability to back date a search by even 1 minute to ascertain arrival times.
(2) Removed ability to learn which track your train is boarding on. This is exceptionally important info at NY Penn and several other stations. It used to be buried and extremely difficult to find on the old version of the app but still available when needed. Now it appears to have been removed entirely.
(3) Train time searches support Depart By function. But there is also an Arrive By function that does not work at all and returns the same search results as Depart By.
The older version of this app was sloppy but still needed. This new version is now completely non-functional except for displaying your ticket to the conductor.

reviews.title: App developers need to take the train to work
reviews.text: This new app update is missing commuter convenience: commuter train live status can no longer be made a favorite and to get to proper screen there’s 4 windows to navigate through (which change depending on geolocation). Since trains are seldom on schedule, this is a much needed feature, especially when standing in the rain, not knowing if the train will arrive at all. Previous version automatically updated live train status - this one requires getting out of the page to reload for update. Also basic app navigation such as swipe left to get to previous screen is missing. Although I appreciate graphic improvements, this revised app is not intuitive and feels like partially-developed beta version. I’m patiently awaiting a meaningful update, just as I’m patiently awaiting the delayed train. * This rating is to motivate the IT team to perform due diligence and is not reflective of the hard work women and men of NJ Transit perform to get us safe to our destinations.

reviews.title: Worst “upgrade” ever
reviews.text:
The new app upgrade feels like a massive downgrade. It honestly feels like we went backwards five years in usability and design.

I genuinely do not understand who approved this redesign. The old app already had issues, but somehow this version is even more cumbersome and harder to navigate. The user experience is terrible HORRID.  

DepartureVision/departures used to be one of the most useful and accessible features in the app, and now it feels buried behind multiple layers of trip navigation just to find basic train information. Everything takes more clicks, more steps, and more effort than it should.

And I work in technology. This is not a case of someone struggling to adapt to a new interface. This is objectively poor UX design. The app feels clunky, overcomplicated, and far less intuitive than the previous version and the previous version was bad but at least slightly better- emphasis on slightly.
This “upgrade” is a huge FAIL and makes me even more frustrated to know the people helped paid for this trash. Do better NJT.

reviews.title: New NJT app
reviews.text: The new interface is awful and more diffuse to find things than the previous platform.  For instance, it takes at least double the clicks to find all the stops in the train and arrival times, if you find your train you do not see the connections which is a real problem it’s like searching for 2 different trains.  If you want to see your train live, you can’t do it anymore.  Nor can you see the different times when a schedule is delayed.  The notifications are months old, just update the current t. It’s clumsy and hard to use than the previous app.  It’s so confusing that frankly it’s taking me much longer to find anything.  Throw it away and start over. It’s bad enough with all the cancellations and delays we endure and now we have an app that stinks.

reviews.title: April 2026 redesign is a big step back
reviews.text:
The NJ Transit app’s recent redesign is a usability failure. Here’s an partial list of ways it got worse:

* Departurevision page no longer shows scheduled departure time if train is within 30 minutes of arriving or “boarding”
* Tracks on Departurevision got unreadably small
* Bottom navbar disappears on some pages, making it useless as a navigation aid
* Getting to a schedule is wildly unintuitive, compared to going to “Schedules” and choosing your stations
* The Trip Planner is a joke, the level of quality you’d expect from a 2009 iPhone app. No one will ever use this 
* Buying a ticket doesn’t remember my last payment method, no way to set a default payment, each time is like my first time using the app
* Entering a transit card CVV (a super common use case) covers the “Submit” button with the number entry keyboard
* Very unclear how to answer the question “Are there any delays on my line?” What’s the difference between a “travel alert” and a “service advisory”?

Any halfway competent software engineer with a $500 Claude budget could easily make a much better version of this app. I would do this myself, but unfortunately only the official app can buy & activate tickets.

reviews.title: New UI update is terrible
reviews.text: I recently updated to the new app with updated UI and it is insanely challenging to find time tables for bus or trains. When trying to see my commute home, the departure vision tries to show me bus or train, when I only want to see train routes. So I need to de-select busses every time. This new update is not user friendly at all. I do not need nj transit to give me a full view of my commute when I walk to the train and then to the destination. I just need to know all the options of my train and how long they take. Genuinely bad update guys. Please revisit this design and make it friendly for users. Give us the departure vision for my specific commute route with an option to quickly look that up

reviews.title: Scheduling issues
reviews.text: I’ve been using this app for a little over 2 years now and I’ve never had an issue with the scheduling. But now, I’m seeing that the updates are very inconsistent. The past month I’ve been waiting for the American dream bus on 32nd bergenline in union city. Why is it saying that there’s no busses in route on the APP, mind you the main source, but on Google Maps it will tell me when the bus is coming? And me, trusting the SOURCE, I would just start walking to work instead of waiting for the next bus that idk when it’s gonna pass because there’s no time on the app. People have work to go to, and the inconsistency is making people late. We need to know what time the busses are passing by. Because why is it that it doesn’t say anything on the app and 2 mins later the bus passes by? What kind of bs is that? I’m sorry but whoever is in charge of scheduling needs to be held accountable. This is very inconsiderate and unprofessional. Do better Jersey.

reviews.title: Terrible in searching stations when buying tickets
reviews.text:
This app is so frustrating to use, to buy tickets, you need to know the mode of transportation, and the zone, or the exact station name. Basically you have to look up the route on google maps first to figure out the mode (lightrail vs train vs bus), then look up the station in the app, then go back to the ticket screen to buy the ticket. And sometimes the station name doesn’t even show up in the list. 
The app should allow users to enter a start and end address, and list the ticket options, instead of requiring users to jump through the hoops and guess which ticket to buy. 
Also there’s no history, so i have to go through the same hassle every few weeks when I visit friends and family in NJ.

reviews.title: No Bus 139 stop at Freehold Raceway Mall
reviews.text:
App is wrong!!! It states there is a stop for Bus 139 at Freehold Raceway Mall to ride into NYC Port Authority. App even tracks the bus saying it stops there. We waited for 30 minutes and bus didn’t come. The sign outside the mall entrance doesn’t list bus 139 and we had to ask another bus driver. We also called NJ transit # on sign and spoke with agent who said it comes to the mall which was also incorrect. Bus drivers and other passengers had to tell us the app is wrong. It delayed our trip significantly because we had to park at mall, wait, then figure out it didn’t come there, get back on car, drive to another bus stop and park, etc.

Please fix the app and remove this stop for 139 bus or have the bus actually go to where the app says.

reviews.title: Convenient when it wants to be.
reviews.text:
This app is great in concept, in that it takes away from the hassle of using paper tickets or cash when you use Nj’s buses or trains.

Honestly, I have no complaints about the apps functionality. 

What i find absolutely ridiculous is the arbitrary one month expiration date when you buy tickets (including when buying in bulk). Granted one can make the argument that “You should know when and where you’re going before hand. Buying a ticket days or weeks in advance is stupid” and I’d counter that but saying I BOUGHT THIS WITH MY MONEY! IT SHOULDNT MATTER WHEN OR HOW LONG IT TAKES ME TO USE IT, ITS MINE. I PAID FOR IT!!

Imagine if you get paid and your employer said “hey this money is good for 30 days, you can only spend this money I’m allowing you to have for a month and if you don’t use it, I assume you don’t want it and I’ll take it back. 

Tickets shouldn’t have expectations or expire. 

My other complaint. You can pre purchase your tickets with every intention to use them as expected. You can be on time, listening to music and watching videos, but when the time comes to activate your ticket, that you paid for and had to login for to use, suddenly you have no connection to the network. You can’t activate your ticket. You can be in Jersey City, Hoboken, Newark, Manhattan, Edison, Plainfield, doesn’t matter. There will come a moment where this thing you’ve depend upon  just won’t work and not let you activate your ticket. 

And sometimes the bus operator or conductor will see
